chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
By Allah, the Shia of Ali (peace be upon him) are none but those who abstain their stomach and private part, and work for their Creator, and hope for His reward, and fear His punishment.

key_terms.فَرْجُهُ: His private part (referring to sexual appetites)

ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of the true Shia of Ali according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to establish that 'Shi'ism' is defined by internal spiritual states rather than mere tribal or political affiliation. The emphasis on 'abstaining from food and private parts' highlights the practical manifestation of *zuhd* (asceticism) and *taqwa* (God-consciousness), while maintaining marital relations), while the dual focus on hope (*raja'*) and fear (*khauf*) reflects the balanced spiritual posture cherished in Shia theology.
